claims.text: A short, controlled annealing treatment can selectively recrystallize the soft fcc phase while retaining a continuous hard B2 phase in a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Selective recrystallization of the fcc phase while retaining the hard-phase skeleton will simultaneously increase tensile strength and ductility relative to the as-cast condition.
Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a lamellar dual-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy containing fcc and B2 phases.
The fcc phase in Al0.7CoCrFeNi is soft and ductile, whereas its B2 phase is hard.
Conventional casting produces the stated lamellar fcc-plus-continuous-B2 initial microstructure.
Annealing temperature and duration can be optimized so that only the fcc phase recrystallizes without changing B2 connectivity.
The intervention will form fine recrystallized grains in the fcc phase alongside a retained networked hard phase.
Phase-selective recrystallization eliminates weak boundaries in the soft phase.
Phase-selective recrystallization enhances or releases the strain-hardening capacity of the duplex microstructure.
The uninterrupted B2 phase provides load-bearing support that preserves strength.
The tailored microstructure activates additional ductility mechanisms.
A phase-selectively recrystallized eutectic high-entropy alloy can exhibit approximately 35% uniform elongation and approximately 2 GPa true stress.
Yield strength and uniform elongation will each improve by approximately 10–20% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The proposed effect should hold under quasi-static loading at a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The improvement requires recrystallization to remain confined to the ductile phase.
Overannealing, hard-phase recrystallization, altered B2 connectivity, or overall coarsening may negate the simultaneous strength-and-ductility benefit.
